expertise.lede: Six fields, each documented in his patents, papers or products.

items.d: Metallocene and single-site catalysts; supported catalysts for gas-phase reactors; catalysts for polyethylene with a bimodal molecular weight distribution.
Polymerisation at supercritical conditions; new polyolefins from the laboratory to scale-up and commercial production; plant and customer troubleshooting.
Chain branching, coil dimensions and melt rheology; polyolefins in the solid and melt state; blends and impact copolymers.
Separator film for lithium-ion batteries, from consumer electronics to transportation; oriented and stretch polyethylene films.
Polyolefin adhesive compositions; vinyl-terminated propylene oligomers as functionalisable building blocks; elastomers and engine-oil additives.
Welding of polypropylene to polyethylene; composite and nanocomposite design, coupling agents and coatings; ring-opening metathesis polymerisation for plugging abandoned wells.

notice.label: Biographical note
notice.title: Biographical <t>note</t>
notice.text: Patrick Brant is a polymer chemist and consultant in polyolefins, based in Houston, Texas. He studied chemistry at George Mason University and took a Ph.D. in inorganic chemistry at the University of Arizona in 1977, followed by post-doctoral research at Purdue University and a National Research Council fellowship at the Naval Research Laboratory in Washington, D.C. He joined Exxon Chemical Company in Baytown, Texas, in 1981, and served ExxonMobil Chemical as Chief Scientist from 2000 to 2011 and as Chief Polymer Science Advisor from 2011 to 2018. His work there included supported metallocene catalysts for gas-phase reactors, the structure–property relationships of polyolefins, and separator film for lithium-ion batteries, developed by a team he led and recognised with the ICIS award for Best Product Innovation in 2008. He is named as inventor on more than 150 US patents and is the author of more than 75 publications. Since 2019 he has worked as an independent consultant and occasional expert witness, collaborates in research with the University of Houston and Baylor University, and founded Molecular Joinery, LLC.
